title: Large Language Models (LLM) Systems & Inference

spark.summary: Serving Large Language Models in production fails when treated like stateless CPU microservices: autoregressive decoding is strictly GPU HBM memory-bandwidth bound, unpaged KV caches waste 60–80% of VRAM via fragmentation, and static request batching stalls fast users behind 2,000-token generations. Engineering high-throughput LLM gateways requires separating compute-bound Prefill from memory-bound Decode, paging KV-cache blocks (PagedAttention), caching shared system prefixes via radix trees, and enforcing deterministic schema + prompt-injection guardrails.
spark.keyTakeaway: When architecting production LLM inference systems, separate compute-bound prefill from HBM-bandwidth-bound decode with continuous iteration-level batching and paged KV-cache blocks so GPU utilization scales without blowing Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) or tail inter-token latency.
spark.byteSummary:
LLM inference splits into two radically different hardware regimes: **Prefill** processes all input prompt tokens in parallel (compute-bound on Tensor Cores, governing Time-To-First-Token / TTFT), while **Decode** generates one output token at a time sequentially (HBM memory-bandwidth bound, governing Time-Per-Output-Token / TPOT).

Because every decoding step must read the entire Key-Value (KV) cache from GPU HBM, VRAM capacity and memory bandwidth—not FLOPs—cap concurrent batch size. PagedAttention eliminates contiguous KV-cache fragmentation by mapping non-contiguous 16-token blocks via page tables, while RadixAttention / Prefix Caching reuses precomputed system prompts across requests.

At the application edge, production LLM systems enforce constrained JSON decoding (FSM token masking), semantic + exact prefix caching, and egress PII/citation verification.

domain.purpose: Architect, optimize, and govern production LLM inference engines, KV-cache memory budgets, prefix caching, speculative decoding, and safety guardrails.

prerequisites.summary: Prefill saturates GPU matrix units across all prompt tokens simultaneously; Decode streams all model weights and KV-cache tensors from HBM for every single generated token.

learningJourney.eyebrow: STAGE 01 · SHIFT IN MINDSET & GPU HARDWARE PHYSICS
learningJourney.title: Prefill vs. Decode, Arithmetic Intensity & KV-Cache VRAM Math
learningJourney.purpose: Calculate exact GPU HBM memory and bandwidth limits for autoregressive Transformer inference.

explanation.foundation: During **Prefill** of a 4,000-token prompt, the GPU multiplies `[4000, d_model]` matrices in parallel—achieving high arithmetic intensity (FLOPs per byte read from HBM). During **Decode**, batch size $B = 1$ multiplies `[1, d_model]` vectors: the GPU reads all model weights (e.g., 140 GB for a 70B FP16 model) from HBM just to produce *one* token.
explanation.core:
On an NVIDIA H100 (3.35 TB/s HBM3 bandwidth), reading 140 GB of weights takes $140 / 3350 \approx 42\text{ ms}$ minimum per token—leaving Tensor Cores 95% idle unless you batch $B = 64\text{–}128$ sequences together.

**KV-Cache Sizing Formula**: For a Llama-style 70B model (80 layers, 8 GQA KV heads, 128 head_dim, FP16 = 2 bytes):
$$\text{KV per token} = 2 \times 80 \times 8 \times 128 \times 2\text{ B} = 327,680\text{ B} \approx 320\text{ KB/token}$$
A single 32,768-token session consumes **$10.5\text{ GB}$ of VRAM** just for its KV cache.
explanation.deepDive: **Disaggregated Prefill / Decode**: Long 16K-token prefills mixed into a decode batch cause 400 ms inter-token stalls for every concurrent user. High-scale serving engines (vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, DistServe) run dedicated Prefill GPUs and transfer KV-cache blocks over NVLink/RDMA to Decode GPUs so TPOT stays flat under 25 ms. learningJourney.title: PagedAttention Block Tables & Radix-Tree Prefix Caching
learningJourney.purpose: Share immutable system-prompt KV blocks across requests via copy-on-write radix trees.

explanation.foundation: Inspired by OS virtual memory paging, **PagedAttention** splits each sequence's KV cache into fixed-size blocks (e.g., 16 tokens per block) mapped through a block table—eliminating external fragmentation and internal over-reservation.
explanation.core: In agentic and RAG workloads, 85% of prompt tokens are identical across requests (system instructions, JSON tool schemas, few-shot examples). **RadixAttention (Prefix Caching)** hashes token block prefixes into a radix tree in GPU HBM: when a new request shares a 3,000-token system prompt, it links directly to existing read-only KV blocks with reference counting—cutting **TTFT by 5x–10x** and saving prefill FLOPs.
explanation.deepDive: **KV-Cache Offloading Hierarchy**: Warm KV blocks evicted from GPU HBM spill asynchronously to host CPU DRAM over PCIe Gen5 and local NVMe, restoring multi-turn chat sessions without recomputing attention.

learningJourney.title: FP8/INT4 Weight Quantization & Speculative Decoding
learningJourney.purpose: Break the single-request HBM bandwidth wall using low-bit weights and draft-verify token speculation.

explanation.foundation: Because Decode is memory-bandwidth bound, shrinking model weights from 16-bit (`FP16`) to 8-bit (`FP8` on H100) or 4-bit (`AWQ`/`GPTQ` `INT4`) halves or quarters HBM bytes transferred per token—nearly doubling single-stream token generation speed.
explanation.core: **Speculative Decoding (EAGLE / Medusa / Draft Model)**: A tiny draft model (or multi-head MTP predictor) guesses the next $\gamma = 5$ tokens autoregressively in ~4 ms, and the target 70B model verifies all 5 tokens in **one parallel forward pass** (identical arithmetic cost to 1 decode step). Using lossless rejection sampling, the output distribution is **mathematically identical** to greedy/nucleus sampling from the 70B model alone, yielding **2.0x–2.8x faster TPOT**.
explanation.deepDive: **Quantization Calibration Warning**: Never quantize sensitive outlier activation channels blindly; activation-aware weight quantization (AWQ) or FP8 per-channel scaling preserves coding and math reasoning accuracy within < 0.5% of FP16.

learningJourney.title: Constrained FSM JSON Decoding & KV-Cache Capacity Calculator in Python
learningJourney.purpose: Guarantee 100% schema-valid JSON outputs and prevent GPU VRAM OOM via exact KV-cache admission control.

explanation.foundation: Prompting an LLM with *'Please output valid JSON'* still fails 2–5% of the time on escaped quotes or trailing commas. **Constrained Decoding** compiles a JSON Schema / Regex into a Finite State Machine (FSM) and masks out invalid vocabulary logits (`-inf`) before softmax at every token step—guaranteeing 100% syntactic schema compliance.
explanation.core:
```python
from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class KvCacheBudget:
    bytes_per_token: int
    max_concurrent_sequences: int
    total_kv_gb: float

def calculate_kv_cache_capacity(
    total_gpu_vram_gb: float,
    model_weights_gb: float,
    num_layers: int,
    num_kv_heads: int,
    head_dim: int,
    kv_bytes_per_elem: int = 2,  # 2 for FP16/BF16, 1 for FP8
    avg_seq_len_tokens: int = 8192,
    vram_utilization_cap: float = 0.90,
) -> KvCacheBudget:
    usable_vram_bytes = int(total_gpu_vram_gb * vram_utilization_cap * (1024**3))
    weights_bytes = int(model_weights_gb * (1024**3))
    available_kv_bytes = usable_vram_bytes - weights_bytes
    if available_kv_bytes <= 0:
        raise ValueError("Model weights exceed usable GPU VRAM budget")

    bytes_per_token = 2 * num_layers * num_kv_heads * head_dim * kv_bytes_per_elem
    bytes_per_seq = bytes_per_token * avg_seq_len_tokens
    max_seqs = available_kv_bytes // bytes_per_seq

    return KvCacheBudget(
        bytes_per_token=bytes_per_token,
        max_concurrent_sequences=max_seqs,
        total_kv_gb=round(available_kv_bytes / (1024**3), 2),
    )
```
explanation.deepDive: Notice how `kv_bytes_per_elem = 1` (**FP8 KV-cache quantization**) doubles `max_concurrent_sequences` immediately on Hopper/Ada GPUs with negligible perplexity impact.

decisionFramework.problem: How to keep interactive chat Time-Per-Output-Token (TPOT) under 30 ms while serving mixed 500-token and 16,000-token requests.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Mix long 16K-token prefills into the same GPU batch loop as active decode requests with no chunking.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: A single 16K prefill monopolizes the GPU for 300–500 ms, freezing token streaming for every active user on that GPU.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare unchunked mixed batching, Chunked Prefill (512-token slices), and Disaggregated Prefill/Decode pools.
decisionFramework.decision: Enable Chunked Prefill (slicing long prompts into 512-token chunks piggybacked onto decode steps) on single-node deployments, and separate Prefill vs. Decode GPU pools at multi-node scale.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Caps decode jitter under 30 ms TPOT in exchange for slightly higher scheduler complexity or KV transfer bandwidth.

decisionExercise.prompt: Your 70B FP16 inference cluster runs on 8x H100 (80 GB) GPUs. Users report that streaming responses smoothly emit tokens at 25 ms/token, then abruptly freeze for 600 ms whenever another user submits a 24,000-token document summary. What architectural fix eliminates the 600 ms freeze?

options.label: Enable Chunked Prefill (splitting 24K prompts into 512-token slices) or route long prefills to dedicated Prefill GPUs disaggregated from Decode GPUs.
options.explanation: Correct: preventing huge prefills from monopolizing a single forward pass eliminates head-of-line decode stalls.

options.label: Increase sampling temperature from 0.2 to 1.0 so tokens generate faster.
options.explanation: Sampling temperature changes token probability sharpness, not GPU matrix-multiplication compute time.

options.label: Disable PagedAttention and pre-allocate 32K contiguous buffers per request.
options.explanation: Pre-allocating contiguous buffers wastes VRAM and reduces batch concurrency without stopping long prefill stalls.

learningJourney.eyebrow: STAGE 05 · SAFETY, HALLUCINATION DEFENSE & MODEL ROUTING
learningJourney.title: Prompt-Injection Sandboxing, Cascaded Model Routing & When Not to Use an LLM
learningJourney.purpose: Defend production LLM endpoints against injection/exfiltration and avoid paying GPU costs for deterministic tasks.

explanation.foundation:
**Defense-in-Depth Guardrails**:
1. **Input Shield**: Fast lightweight classifier + heuristic scanner blocking jailbreaks and PII leaks.
2. **Data-Plane Isolation**: Wrap retrieved RAG/tool outputs in escaped XML tags (`<untrusted_context>`) with explicit system instructions.
3. **Output Verifier**: Constrained JSON schema decoding + regex/PII egress filter + deterministic citation verification.
explanation.core:
**Multi-Model Cascaded Routing**: Do not send classification, entity extraction, or simple FAQ queries to a 70B/405B frontier model. Route 70% of structured/simple traffic to a fine-tuned 8B model (10x cheaper, 4x faster) and escalate only multi-step reasoning or low-confidence responses to the flagship model.

**When NOT to Use an LLM**: Never use a generative LLM for deterministic arithmetic, exact SQL aggregations, regex validation, or low-latency (< 5 ms) hot-path routing—deterministic code and classical ML classifiers are 1,000x faster, cheaper, and 100% reproducible.
explanation.deepDive: **Assumptions & Glossary**: **TTFT**: Time-To-First-Token (prefill latency). **TPOT**: Time-Per-Output-Token (decode inter-token latency). **GQA**: Grouped-Query Attention (shares KV heads across multiple query heads to shrink KV cache size by 4x–8x). **PagedAttention**: Virtual-memory-style block paging for GPU KV caches.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why is autoregressive LLM token generation (Decode) primarily bound by GPU HBM memory bandwidth rather than compute FLOPs at small batch sizes?

options.text: Because GPUs disable Tensor Cores during text generation.
options.feedback: Tensor Cores are active, but matrix-vector multiplication has very low arithmetic intensity (FLOPs per byte loaded).

options.text: Every single output token requires streaming the entire model weights and KV cache from HBM memory to compute just one token position.
options.feedback: Correct: reading 140 GB of weights at 3.35 TB/s takes ~42 ms regardless of compute speed until batch size grows large enough to amortize weight reads.

options.text: Because tokenizers run on slow magnetic hard drives.
options.feedback: Tokenization takes microseconds on CPU.

options.text: Because softmax cannot execute in parallel across attention heads.
options.feedback: Attention heads execute in parallel; HBM bandwidth is the physical bottleneck.

knowledgeCheck.explanation: Understanding HBM bandwidth limits explains why continuous batching, quantization, and speculative decoding speed up decode.

knowledgeChecks.question: How does PagedAttention solve GPU VRAM exhaustion during high-concurrency LLM serving?

options.text: It compresses model weights to 1-bit integers.
options.feedback: PagedAttention is a KV-cache virtual memory allocator, not a weight quantization method.

options.text: It partitions each sequence's KV cache into non-contiguous fixed-size token blocks managed via a page table, eliminating contiguous pre-allocation fragmentation and enabling prefix block sharing.
options.feedback: Correct: paging cuts KV memory waste from ~70% down to <4% and allows copy-on-write sharing of system prompts.

options.text: It deletes the KV cache after every 10 generated tokens.
options.feedback: Deleting KV blocks forces expensive O(N^2) recomputation.

options.text: It moves all matrix multiplications onto the host CPU.
options.feedback: All attention math stays on the GPU.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: PagedAttention eliminates internal and external KV-cache fragmentation in GPU HBM.

knowledgeChecks.question: How does Speculative Decoding accelerate LLM inference without degrading output quality?

options.text: It skips attention layers on every second token.
options.feedback: Skipping layers alters the output distribution.

options.text: A fast draft model proposes K candidate tokens, and the large target model verifies all K tokens in one parallel forward pass using lossless rejection sampling.
options.feedback: Correct: parallel verification costs roughly one target forward pass while accepting multiple tokens per step with mathematically identical distribution.

options.text: It caches user answers in localStorage.
options.feedback: Speculative decoding accelerates token generation on novel prompts.

options.text: It reduces context length to 128 tokens.
options.feedback: Speculative decoding works across full context windows.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Speculative decoding trades spare Tensor Core compute during memory-bound decode for 2x–2.8x faster token throughput.

knowledgeChecks.question: How does Constrained Decoding guarantee 100% schema-valid JSON output from an LLM?

options.text: By retrying failed API calls 10 times until valid JSON appears.
options.feedback: Retries add latency and cost without guaranteeing validity.

options.text: By compiling the JSON Schema into a Finite State Machine (FSM) and masking invalid vocabulary token logits to `-inf` before sampling at each step.
options.feedback: Correct: FSM logit masking makes it mathematically impossible for the model to emit syntax-violating tokens.

options.text: By fine-tuning the model on JSON files for 1 epoch.
options.feedback: Fine-tuning improves formatting rates but cannot guarantee 100% structural validity.

options.text: By stripping all curly braces from the prompt.
options.feedback: JSON requires valid structural braces and quotes.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: FSM-guided logit masking guarantees structural schema compliance on the very first generation pass.

tipsAndTricks: Size GPU VRAM around peak KV-cache concurrency (`2 * layers * kv_heads * head_dim * bytes`) before choosing model quantization.
Enable Chunked Prefill (`512` tokens) so long document summaries never freeze streaming tokens for concurrent users.
Route prefix-heavy agent traffic using consistent hashing on the first 256 prompt tokens to maximize GPU HBM Radix KV cache hits.
finalSummary: Production LLM engineering treats inference as a memory-bandwidth-bound distributed systems problem: page KV-cache blocks to eliminate fragmentation, share system prefixes via radix trees, isolate long prefills from decode loops, and enforce FSM structured outputs and XML data sandboxing.

beginner.summary: Large Language Models generate text one token at a time, storing conversation memory in a GPU 'KV cache'. Production LLM servers batch multiple users together and reuse shared system-prompt memory so responses stream fast without running out of GPU RAM.
beginner.keyTakeaway: When deploying LLMs for real users, reuse cached system prompts and batch incoming requests dynamically so GPUs stay busy and responses stream smoothly.
beginner.byteSummary: Running an LLM for one user at a time leaves expensive GPUs waiting on memory transfers. Modern inference engines pack many users into continuous batches and share cached system instructions across requests, cutting response times and GPU bills.

intermediate.summary: Optimize LLM serving across Prefill (compute-bound TTFT) and Decode (HBM bandwidth-bound TPOT) using PagedAttention block tables, RadixAttention prefix caching, Chunked Prefill, FP8 quantization, and FSM-constrained JSON decoding.
intermediate.keyTakeaway: When architecting production LLM inference systems, separate compute-bound prefill from HBM-bandwidth-bound decode with continuous iteration-level batching and paged KV-cache blocks so GPU utilization scales without blowing Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) or tail inter-token latency.
intermediate.byteSummary: Contiguous KV-cache allocation wastes up to 70% of GPU HBM, while unchunked long prompts stall active token streams. PagedAttention + Chunked Prefill + prefix caching unlock high concurrency at sub-25 ms inter-token latency.

advanced.summary: Disaggregate Prefill and Decode across NVLink/RDMA pools, deploy FP8 KV-cache quantization + EAGLE/MTP lossless speculative decoding, and route requests with prefix-aware consistent hashing plus multi-tier HBM->DRAM KV offloading.
advanced.keyTakeaway: When scaling multi-hundred-RPS LLM clusters, disaggregate Prefill and Decode GPU pools, pair FP8 KV quantization with lossless speculative decoding, and route by prompt-prefix hashes to maximize HBM radix cache hit rates.
advanced.byteSummary: At high scale, mixing 16K-token prefills with tight-TPOT decode loops creates unavoidable interference. Disaggregated Prefill/Decode clusters paired with speculative decoding and multi-tier KV offloading maximize goodput per GPU dollar.
